title: add benchmark-lab performance suites, profiling baselines, representative runners, and reporting pipeline v118
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes:
- Add new performance test suites (latency, throughput, mixed workloads)
- Add profiling baselines for v118 (cold start, steady-state)
- Introduce representative workload runners for multimodal batch tests
- Reporting pipeline: ETL + dashboarding updates and daily aggregation jobs
description:
Context: benchmark-lab v118 combines new performance suites, updated profiling baselines, representative workload runners, and an updated reporting pipeline to improve baseline capture and daily telemetry aggregation. Motivation: recent customer incidents and internal perf regressions (ENG-7821) exposed gaps in our baseline capture (cold-start vs steady-state) and made it difficult to compare results across model variants. This PR adds standardized suites, a canonical baseline set for v118, representative runners for mixed and multi-variant workloads, and a resilient reporting pipeline that tolerates transient infra failures.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds three new performance test suites: latency_small_seq, throughput_mixed_load, and multimodal_batching. These are templated and parameterized for runner reuse.
- Introduces profiling baselines for v118 across GPU shapes (A100-40GB, A100-80GB, and T4) including cold-start, warm-start, and long-run memory traces. Baselines include trace artifacts and summary CSVs.
- Implements representative workload runners that emulate production traffic patterns (token distributions, prompt prefixes, KV cache warmup). Runners support both synthetic and captured-trace modes.
- Updates the reporting pipeline: adds robust ETL steps, incremental aggregation (daily/hourly), and new dashboard metrics (p50/p95 latency by model+variant, cost-per-token, batch-efficiency). Pipeline job definitions include retry/backoff and dead-letter handling.
- Adds tests and CI jobs to run a lightweight subset of suites on PRs to catch obvious regressions.

Checklist:
- [x] Add performance suites and runner templates
- [x] Add profiling baseline artifacts and metadata
- [x] Add reporting pipeline ETL and aggregation jobs
- [x] Wire up nightly jobs and cloud storage retention policy
- [x] Update docs/benchmark-lab/README with usage and how to add new suites

Backward compatibility: No breaking changes to public APIs. New runners and baselines are additive. Reporting pipeline changes are additive and behind feature flags for rollout.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for runner orchestration and config parsing included.
- Integration test for reporting pipeline uses a local emulated run; CI runs smoke subset.
- Manual validation: ran full suites against a staging cluster for A100-80GB and validated aggregated dashboard output and baseline CSV compatibility.

Risks and mitigations:
- Large baseline artifacts increase storage usage - mitigated by lifecycle policy (30d hot, 365d archive) and dedup strategies.
- Reporting pipeline transient failures - mitigated by retries and dead-letter queue with alerting.

Related: ENG-7821 (perf regression triage), ENG-7899 (benchlab infra improvements), SUP-412 (support ticket that motivated cold-start baselines).
